newsitem.title: USA: Price hike could help General Mills meet EPS goal.
newsitem.headline: Price hike could help General Mills meet EPS goal.

text.p: General Mills Corp's surprise 2.6 percent cereal price increase announced late Wednesday could go a long way toward it's goal of increasing earnings by about $0.30 a share this year, according to industry analysts.
For the fiscal year ended in May, General Mills reported $3.00 per share in earnings, excluding a one-time charge.

The cereal price increase would amount to about a $0.22-a-share gain in earnings, leaving room for General Mills to increase marketing and price promotions, said Schroder and Co analyst Robert Cummins.
"It gives them a head start and even if they spend half of it and keep 11 cents, that still gives them a good cushion," he said.
In fact, without the price increase, Minneapolis-based General Mills might not have reached its earnings target, said Nomi Ghez, analyst at Goldman Sachs.
"Frankly, I believe that General Mills recognized that it would not be able to achieve its earnings per share for the new fiscal year without raising prices," Ghez said.
Analysts said they are watching with keen interest to see whether General Mills follows the price rise with an increase in discount coupon offers.
In the early 1990s, when cereal companies would raise prices, they would then try to attract consumers with discount coupons.
"Whether this means a return to this pattern is the big question," said Bankers Trust analyst John O'Neil.
Some analysts said that pattern hurt the value of the company's brands. In more recent years, cereal companies have been cutting prices and cutting back on promotional spending.
General Mills did not say if the price increase would be followed by increased promotion and discount coupons.
Ghez noted that in a meeting with analysts last week, General Mills emphasized building the value of its brands and advertising over price promotion.
In raising its cereal prices, General Mills broke ranks with its ready-to-eat cereal competitors. While none have yet announced increases, some analysts said they expect they will.
"My guess at this point is the whole industry would go for a price increase," Ghez said.

Industry-leader Kellogg Co might increase prices only on selected brands, while Quaker Oats Co and Post Cereal, a part of Philip Morris Co Inc's Kraft Foods unit, would be likely to raise prices across the board, she noted.

Analysts mostly reacted favorably to the General Mills price increase, a sentiment reflected in cereal stock prices Friday. General Mills was up 2-3/16 at 67-15/16, Kellogg was up 4-7/8 at 91-7/8 and Quaker Oats was up 3/4 at 45-7/8.
